title: Clearer work. Stronger follow-through.
lead: Overhead LLC develops OverHead, a Windows-centered business workspace that brings customer context, daily tasks, quotes, invoices, and approvals into one operating view.

pages.title: The opportunity
pages.body: Businesses lose time when the next action is scattered across inboxes, spreadsheets, calendars, and staff conversations. Quotes wait, payment follow-up slips, and owners become the routing system for routine decisions. OverHead addresses the administrative work between a customer inquiry and a completed outcome: knowing what needs attention, who owns it, and what happens next.

pages.title: The product
pages.body: OverHead combines an installed Windows workspace with a shared account and browser layer. Its operating tools bring customer records, tasks, quote and invoice status, follow-up, and approval queues within reach of the people doing the work. Role controls, activity records, local documents, and backup tools support accountability and continuity. The value proposition is practical: less time reconstructing context and a clearer path to finishing work.

pages.title: Universal by design. Focused in execution.
pages.body: OverHead is built around administrative needs shared across industries, rather than a single trade. The business plan proposes owner-led service offices as an initial route to customer validation, not a limit on who the product can serve. Early adoption should begin with one recurring workflow, then expand as the organization sees value.

pages.title: Why OverHead
pages.body: The product brings operational context and the next action together. A Windows-first workspace keeps daily work close to the desk, while shared identity, permissions, and browser access connect the wider team. Its intended advantage is a consistent operating routine: capture the work, assign responsibility, review sensitive actions, and retain the history needed to explain the outcome.

pages.title: The business model
pages.body: The plan centers on recurring workspace subscriptions. Published desktop tiers are Silver at $59, Gold at $129, and Black at $299 per month, with a one-time 90-day Gold trial. Cylinder is a separate Windows Server and Windows IoT deployment option. These offers define the commercial model; production billing acceptance and paid customer traction remain to be verified.

pages.title: A product foundation already in place
pages.body: The existing foundation includes a packaged desktop application, public website, account and onboarding flows, operating workflows, product documentation, customer and investor brochures, and a detailed business plan with an editable financial model. This is evidence of product development and preparation. Customer adoption, recurring revenue, and measured productivity gains have not been independently established in the materials supporting this summary.

pages.title: A disciplined path to growth
pages.body: The plan proposes validating a small pilot cohort before scaling acquisition. Success should be measured through completed setup, repeat weekly use, faster follow-through, willingness to pay, and retention. Commercial readiness includes verified billing, trusted software distribution, and tested recovery. Expansion should follow demonstrated customer value, with integrations and workflow improvements guided by observed use.

pages.title: Financial approach
pages.body: The companion workbook models 36 months across downside, base, and upside scenarios. Its base case assumes $175,000 in opening capital, a $126.50 monthly subscription mix, and 2% monthly customer churn. These are illustrative planning inputs, not actual sales, existing cash, a company valuation, or an approved funding request. Spending and growth commitments should follow validated demand and available resources.

closing: Overhead LLC’s objective is to turn a developed software foundation into a dependable business: help organizations complete everyday work with greater clarity, then earn growth through sustained use and customer trust.
